pr_title: fix: Table editor deleting / pagination bug
pr_body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Fixes #9305

## Bug Fix
Table should reload with the correct row data once all the records on the current page is deleted.
## What is the current behavior?
Deleting 100 rows in the table leaves the table in a weird state, requiring a refresh. At first, it looks like you've deleted all of your rows, not just the 100 you selected.

## What is the new behavior?
Table loads with the correct data rows once the first 100 rows are loaded without requiring a refresh.

## Demo
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/51731962/233307574-22e3542b-29e9-4924-8afe-da12e73a1830.mov


---

issue_context.title: Table editor deleting / pagination bug
issue_context.body:
# Bug report

Deleting 100 rows in the table leaves the table in a weird state, requiring a refresh.  At first, it looks like you've deleted all of your rows, not just the 100 you selected. 

**To reproduce**

Create a new table with a lot of rows:

1. Go to the SQL editor → Welcome page → Quick start section → Countries to quickly create a table with a lot of entries
2. Go to that new countries table
3. Select all rows at the top, then Delete 100 rows
 
![CleanShot 2022-10-03 at 13 07 32@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/105593/193620752-1b0fbcc8-b3a5-4919-a672-4f805596b35c.png)
4. Notice that your table empty. It looks like the entire table content has been deleted, but that's not the case. 
![CleanShot 2022-10-03 at 13 18 02@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/105593/193621162-28f9c00b-02d3-429c-8dae-e9e46a34c1bd.png)
comments: The issue was that the react-query queries were not invalidated properly after deleting rows. This is now fixed.

review_comments: @joshenlim when `REMOVE_ROWS` is dispatched, `rows` and `totalRows` are already updated.
